applied.change: Corrected the printed promise from the real output rather than from memory, and kept the check that found it. `bash test.sh` now promises `passed 19, failed 0`, which is what it prints.

Re-ran the deliberate breakage and recorded the measured result in both the README and provenance.json: `passed 17, failed 2` broken, `passed 19, failed 0` restored. The guess matched, and is recorded here as a guess that matched rather than quietly kept.

Built tools/named_proof.py for the example corpus and wired it into tools/phase.py as the `named proof` and `named proof self-test` gates. Arm (a): every quote sharing a paragraph with a record id is matched against that record's snippet or read and typed exact / formatting / drifted / absent, the last two blocking. Arm (c): every printed command in a fenced block whose promise contains a number is run as written from the area directory and the promise must appear in its real output. Proven by --selftest, which plants a quote with an altered tail and a promise of `passed 999, failed 0` and requires both caught -- the self-test exists because the previous ceremony learned that `wired` without `proven able to fail` is satisfiable by a no-op. Five attributed quotes in the live area now verify exact where nothing read them before.

Closed 75-boundary-ask-watch-steer on arms (a) and (c) with its original text preserved under sharper_check_original, and split arms (b) and (d) into lesson 13b-named-proof-bd with its own sharper_check saying what each would take and which to build first -- (b), because it has a recorded catch and (d) does not. The loop ranks the remainder instead of the parent reading as finished.

note: The item worked in this phase was selected by `tools/improvement_loop.py plan 1`, not chosen by the author. That is the first time a plan fired by the loop has driven a phase end to end: the loop ranked a lesson that had already cost a recurrence, the phase built the tool, the loop's own check verified the stop condition mechanically, and the tool found a real defect in the repo's worked example on its first run.
